chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, from 'Umar ibn Yazeed, who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'In the Book of Ali (peace be upon him), the drinker of wine is to be whipped, and the drinker of the intoxicant.' I said, 'How much?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Their penalty (Hadd) is one (and the same).'
ai.seo_question: What is the prescribed penalty for drinking wine and other intoxicants in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the legal equivalence between wine (khamr) and all other intoxicants (muskir) regarding the hadd penalty, grounding the ruling in the authority of Imam Ali (AS). It highlights the Shia scholarly tradition of deriving specific jurisprudential details from the Prophet's and Imams' direct interpretations of the Quran and their own writings, confirming that the distinction in type does not alter the fixed corporal punishment of flogging.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Abu Nasr, from hammad Bin Usman, from Umar Bin Yazeed who said,

‘I heard Abu Abdullahasws saying: ‘In the Book of Aliasws, a drinker of the wine is to be whipped, and a drinker of the intoxicant’. I said, ‘How much?’ Heasws said: ‘Their Penalty (Hadd) is one (and the same)’.
